summary: The study investigated the effects of the modified ZhuJing pill (mZJP) on dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), and immunofluorescence in dry AMD model mice. The analysis of mZJP's chemical metabolites revealed 113 major metabolites, and the results showed that mZJP alleviated retinal pathological alterations and inhibited epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) progression. The study also found that mZJP's EMT-suppressing effect was significantly attenuated upon Nrf2 silencing, suggesting that Nrf2 activation and inhibition of the Akt/GSK-3β pathway are crucial for RPE protection against oxidative stress induced EMT.
